messages:
Jason M.: Heads up — seeing a tail latency bump in eu-west-1 between ~21:12-21:17. Correlates with dedicated pool handoffs. Warm-pool prefill + pool handshake looks like it's racing and triggering fallback routing -> extra egress and higher cost. Anyone else noticing?
Priya K.: Yup, noticed the same on dashboards. handshake_fail_rate and fallback_routing_count spike at 21:13. GPU util stayed normal, networking looked noisy around the proxy.
infra-bot: ALERT: routing-handshake-failure detected (eu-west-1). group=dedicated-handshake count=47 window=5m severity=warning
Jason M.: Logs snippet: `ERROR route.handshake: timeout=15000ms from pool-A->pool-B, reason="session_mismatch"` — looks like the proxy handshake sometimes doesn't accept the new slot before traffic shifts.
Emma S.: Repro steps I tried: repeated short inference bursts with keepalive sockets + warmup traffic. After a warm-pool advertise, some requests immediately get routed to fallback variants. Seems like advertise happens before target can fully accept KV state.
Maya R.: We enabled `prefer-warm` flag in rollout 2 days ago to reduce cold-starts. Could be that advertise is too eager and causes race.
Lukas T.: Sounds like a timing window issue. Two quick mitigations: back off advertise (delay) or add a soft-quarantine period where newly-advertised slots are treated conservatively for routing. I prefer soft-quarantine so we keep warm benefits but avoid immediate promotion.
Priya K.: Metrics to watch for the canary: `handshake_fail_rate`, `fallback_routing_count`, `egress_tx_bytes`, per-tenant tail latency (p99). Also watch tenant `search` — they showed most of the fallback traffic in the spike.
Jason M.: Proposed quick patch (will canary): 
```
# config/route.yml diff
route:
  handshake:
    timeout_ms: 12000
    soft_quarantine_sec: 30
warmup:
  advertise_delay_sec: 15
```
This shortens timeout a bit, adds a 30s quiet window, and delays advertise by 15s.
Emma S.: Quick question — could `soft_quarantine` increase queuing and therefore tail latency for users during the window? We should simulate with loadgen first.
Maya R.: Ran a micro-test earlier with `prefer-warm` disabled on a small canary rack — fallback_count dropped ~70% and p99 improved slightly. No big queueing observed in short tests.
Lukas T.: Plan: 1) rollback `prefer-warm` on eu-west canary group OR set advertise_delay=15s; 2) deploy handshake soft_quarantine + reduced timeout to canary-3; 3) run synthetic tail load for 30m; 4) if stable, roll to remainder. Any objections? @Maya R. @Priya K.
Priya K.: :thumbsup: go ahead. Also open INFRA ticket and add SRE runbook link for monitoring.
Jason M.: Created INFRA-2398 and linked the runbook (https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-2398). Pushing config to canary now, will ping when started.
infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT: config/route v2.14 -> canary-3 started by Jason M. at 21:40 UTC
Priya K.: Canary metrics after 10m: handshake_fail_rate down 0.9% -> 0.2%; fallback_routing_count down ~65%; egress_tx_bytes normalized (previous spike cleared). Cost delta small (+0.5%) during transition but expected to reduce after no fallbacks.
Emma S.: Good signal. Put 30m watch on eu-west and keep an eye on tenant `search` quotas.
Jason M.: Thanks — if stable we'll roll gradually. Follow-ups: add explicit healthcheck handshake ack in proxy (longer-term), and add unit test for advertise/accept race. I'll schedule a short postmortem if we see recurrence.
Maya R.: FYI I'll draft a tiny runbook update for warmup flags and handoff tuning.
Lukas T.: Also consider metric alert for sudden increase in `fallback_routing_count` per-tenant so we can auto-throttle advertise.
Jason M.: Noted. Closing the loop here — will report back after 30m.
Priya K.: Confirmed — 30m watch started.
Jason M.: Ping: canary remained stable at 30m. Preparing to rollout to the rest of eu-west with staged batches. Thanks team!
